content.comment_body: Hello, I would like to write to the internal memory of the [product_name] (hardware type [article_no]) by sending commands online from my PC via a standard TCP/IP socket connection. My goal is to modify the delay setting of a Retentive On-Delay Block while the system is running. Is this feasible, and if so, which port should be used for the connection? Thank you.
You might want to try additional software like the one at [url] or this German resource at [url].

analysis.insight_summary: The user is looking for a method to programmatically adjust internal memory settings, specifically for a Retentive On-Delay Block in [product_name] hardware using TCP/IP socket communication from a PC. Since official products do not directly support this function, users refer to potential third-party solutions. There is a notable lack of straightforward official information or tools for this requirement.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to be able to modify [product_name] [article_no] parameters directly from a PC and wishes to utilize standard TCP/IP protocols for this online operation.
